waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target. requires_doctor_input is true: with advanced liver disease, ascites, swelling, heart or kidney disease, pregnancy or water pills (diuretics such as spironolactone) the app shows only the general range and never pushes a higher target; fluid limits in advanced liver disease are set by the doctor. Choose water, plain chaas and unsweetened drinks; avoid soft drinks, packaged juice, sharbat, sweet lassi, alcohol and herbal liver-detox drinks. Follow your doctor's advice.

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose fatty liver or judge liver scarring; blood tests, ultrasound and often a FibroScan reviewed by a doctor are needed.

The app never suggests starting, stopping or changing any medicine or supplement (vitamin E, pioglitazone, semaglutide, resmetirom, statins, diabetes or BP medicines, omega-3 capsules, herbal products). Follow your doctor.
No alcohol is advised. Do not stop heavy drinking suddenly without medical advice.

Vitamin E at 800 IU/day is a doctor-only option for selected biopsy-proven NASH; reports link long-term use with a small prostate cancer rise and possible higher mortality at high doses. The app has no vitamin E preset.
Herbal, Ayurvedic and 'liver detox' products, and concentrated extracts of turmeric, green tea, ashwagandha or giloy, have been linked to liver injury; show any such product to your doctor.
Coffee has only observational links with less liver scarring; it is not a treatment and the app sets no cups target. Keep it unsweetened.
Emergency: vomiting blood, black stools, new confusion or extreme drowsiness, severe belly pain or fever with a swollen belly, chest pain or stroke signs. Seek emergency care now (112).
Talk to your doctor for yellow eyes or skin, dark urine, a swollen belly or legs, easy bruising, FIB-4 of 1.3 or more, or a FibroScan above about 8 kPa.
With advanced liver disease, heart or kidney disease, pregnancy or diuretics, follow your doctor's advice on fluids and salt; potassium salt substitutes are not shown.

requires_doctor_input is true because fatty liver can hide scarring, many users take diabetes, BP or cholesterol medicines and diuretics, and protein, fluid and sodium needs change in advanced disease; the app sets only general food, sugar, alcohol, sodium, activity and weight guidance on its own.
